after: Are you working out at home but seeing zero results? As a certified personal trainer, I see the same three mistakes ruin home workouts. First, the random workout trap. You search for a quick fifteen-minute session on a whim. It feels good, but your body adapts. If you change every day, tracking progress is hard. To build strength, you need progressive overload. That just means making things slightly harder. With body weight, add one more rep next week or rest thirty seconds less. Pick a simple routine and stick to it for four to six weeks. That is how you grow. Second mistake, you are rushing. When we do not have heavy weights, we tend to fly through exercises. We bounce at the bottom of our squats. We drop like a stone in our push-ups. But when you rush, gravity does the work, not your muscles. Let's fix that with tempo. Next time you squat, take a full three seconds to lower down. Pause for one second at the bottom. Then stand back up. Controlling that movement increases the time your muscles are working. It is a key way to build strength with zero equipment. Third, your space is not set up for success. If you try to exercise two feet from your TV with your phone lighting up on the floor, you will lose focus. Your brain thinks the living room is for relaxing. Clear a dedicated zone. Move the coffee table. Put your phone in another room. A physical boundary helps your mind shift into workout mode.
